**ffmpeg (exactly 10.00 s, frame-accurate):**
```
ffmpeg -ss 10 -i jet-30s.mp4 -t 10 -c:v libx264 -crf 16 -c:a aac -b:a 192k highlight.mp4
```
This keeps the same framing and the original audio track, and adds no text or effects. The video is re-encoded at very high quality so the cut starts on the exact frame. A faster `-c copy` cut can be off by a fraction of a second.

**CapCut / Photos / iMovie:** set the start at 0:10 and the end at 0:20, and add no effects or text. Export at the original resolution.

That gives you one continuous 10-second highlight from 0:10 to 0:20 with your original sound and framing. I didn't run any Magic Hour jobs, so no credits were used.
